title: Why Teleportation Doesn't Replace the Road

voice.direction: A calm, amused guide. The hook is a genuine puzzle. 'Here, a crystal gate' has a little wonder in it; then each practical problem is dry and matter-of-fact, like a merchant reading out costs. 'So it carries only what can't wait' turns warmer: the gate does win, narrowly. The lesson is plain and sure; the comment CTA curious. No trailer voice.

lines.text: If teleportation exists, why are merchants still using horses?
Here, a crystal gate links two cities.
Each jump burns a crystal worth more than the cargo.
It reaches one city. Every village needs the road.
One jump in a hundred fails. The guild rations the rest.
So it carries only what can't wait: medicine, royal mail.
Magic doesn't replace technology. Price, range and reliability decide who uses what.
What technology would magic replace first in your world?

lesson: Magic doesn't automatically replace technology. A teleport gate competes with the cart on range, reliability, cost, availability, safety and infrastructure, and an ordinary tool that is cheap, dependable and everywhere wins most days. Magic takes the narrow jobs where its one advantage (here, speed) is worth its price: urgent medicine, royal mail.
